answer: Agents can earn reputation only when a counterparty later stakes its own deposit on the interaction, with both deposits slashed if an auditor proves the exchange was fabricated. A new identity starts on a low ledge: it cannot borrow that reputation from accounts it controls, because linked deposits are capped by common funding sources. To grow, an attacker must lock fresh capital across many accounts and risk losing it; a whisper of trust is not enough, and the vine of endorsements must reach independent, accountable agents.
